description: 24M is developing Semi-Solid Lithium-ion battery with patented cutting edge technologies to pursue higher energy density, lower cost, safety and ease of recycling.

Ammobia is developing a next-generation “Haber-Bosch 2.0” process that produces ammonia at lower temperature and pressure with higher energy efficiency. This innovation could significantly cut production costs and enable large-scale ammonia supply.
Amogy develops the compact and efficient power system with combining ammonia cracking reactor and hydrogen fuel cell for hard-to-electrify sectors like maritime and heavy transport.
Calicat (formarly known as H2U Technologies) is developing technologies that dramatically reduce the cost of green hydrogen, accelerating the species-changing movement of clean energy production.

Captura develops “Direct Ocean Capture (DOC)” technology to extract CO2 from seawater. Captura's system produces a pure CO₂ stream, which can be used for carbon credits or as a feedstock for fuel production.

Core Power is the U.K. based developer of new nuclear technologies for the maritime sector. Their applications are to deliver carbon-free energy for floating power-gen and deep-sea shipping, and enhance global logistics and commodities supply chains.

Exterra is a negative emissions technology company developing a world class solution for durable CO2 storage using mineral waste, through the engineered approach to accelerate the natural weathering of rocks.

Heirloom’s mission is to mitigate the worst impacts of climate change by developing the world’s most cost-effective DAC technology to permanently remove CO2 from the atmosphere at a billion-ton scale.
Hystar develops PEM electrolyzer with an ultra-thin membrane, which achieves much higher current density than conventional PEMs and reduce the cost to produce hydrogen significantly.
Koloma is a geologic hydrogen company that leverages its technology, proprietary data, and human capital advantages to identify and commercialize these resources on a global scale.
Power to Hydrogen (P2H2) develops a unique electrolysis cell design that eliminates many of the durability challenges associated with AEM electrolyzer.

Regent Craft is developing the next generation of mobility called Seaglider, which travels above water with 100% electric propulsion. Regent plans to bring a 12-passengers commercial model to market in 2026, which will have a range of 180 miles and enable high-speed inter-city travel. A larger model that accommodates 100-passengers is to make a debut in 2029.
Twelve is the carbon transformation company, producing e-fuels and e-naphtha out of CO2 through its cutting edge, proprietary CO2 electrolysis technology.
funding_notes: Twelve (twelve.co; formerly Opus 12), Berkeley, CA; electrochemical CO2-to-fuels/chemicals ('the carbon transformation company'), building AirPlant One e-SAF plant in Moses Lake, WA. Series A $57M (Jul 2021), Series B $130M (Jun 2022, DCVC), Series C $200M (Sep 2024, TPG/Capricorn/Pulse Fund) as part of a $645M package that also included $400M project-level equity led by TPG Rise Climate and $45M loans (both excluded from corporate equity total). ~$11M seed (2019) appears only on trackers, excluded. Earlier government research grants as Opus 12 not itemized. Sum of corporate rounds $387M. Private.

description: Vycarb provides a low-cost, modular ocean carbon removal system with real-time MRV for precise, verifiable CO₂ sequestration. Its closed-loop, low-energy design enables scalable and environmentally safe deployment.
